summary: The @lhd/web Next.js App Router app meets every requirement: non-throwing @lhd/shared-typed API client, all four routes with full Phase rendering and readable domain labels, accessible semantic markup, the 'strengthens and never replaces' philosophy in UI copy, and independently re-verified offline build (0 errors), clean lint, and 21 passing tests; scope is confined to apps/web plus additive root scripts with all protected packages untouched.

findings.detail: Test runner is Jest via next/jest rather than the contract-mandated Vitest, because the workspace absolute path ends in '%' which makes Vite's decodeURI throw URIError and prevents Vitest from collecting tests. The deviation is documented in VERIFICATION.md and FEAT-001, coverage is equivalent (21 tests, 3 suites, all passing), and it does not affect next build. Accepted as a justified environmental workaround; no action required unless the repo is relocated to a '%'-free path.

Page-level server components (app/**/page.tsx) and the assistant's interactive submit/loading/error state transitions have no direct unit tests; they are exercised only indirectly by the recorded runtime HTML probe. Low risk given their thinness, but adding a lightweight assistant-form interaction test would close the gap.

Reviewer independently reproduced offline build (0 errors, API down), lint (clean), and tests (21 passing). The runtime HTML probe (check 4) was accepted from the recorded evidence in VERIFICATION.md rather than re-run, since the probe script was deleted per the task instructions.
